newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage backeds slip, narrow to Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage backeds slip, narrow to Treasuries.

text.p: Widespread buying supported U.S. mortgage-backed securities through much of Wednesday's session, but prices of both mortgages and Treasuries slid lower late in the afternoon, traders said.
At 1530 EST/2030 GMT, mortgages were off 1/32 to 4/32 overall, while comparable Treasuries were down 3/32 to 7/32. Yield spreads between the two markets were unchanged to moderately narrower.
"Mortgages have done pretty well," one trader said. "We saw a lot of buying earlier."
Dollar roll plays abounded, market experts said. "People bought 8.0s and 8.5s," said one Ginnie Mae trader.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was off 3/32 at 100-14/32 bid, yielding 105 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae issues were off 2/32 at 100-10/32 bid, while Freddie Mac 7.5s were down 3/32 at 100-12/32.
The 10-year note was off 7/32 at 100-9/32, yielding 6.46 percent.
